posts.title: 《Yesterday Once More》批判性阅读素材
posts.text: 编者按（Cheukwang Hau）：这是英语写作 / 批判性阅读课程《Yesterday Once More》单元的阅读素材——一份歌词讲义，附带版权与合理使用说明。出于版权考虑，本篇不逐字转载整首歌词，仅保留引用信息、合理使用说明与少量节选，并附上我作为编者的点评。完整歌词请通过正规音乐平台或实体唱片获取。 歌曲信息 曲名：Yesterday Once More 表演：Carpenters（卡朋特乐队） 年份：1973 词曲：Richard Carpenter & John Bettis 收录专辑：Now & Then（A&M Records, 1973） 引用格式MLA 9th ed. Carpenter, Richard, and John Bettis. “Yesterday Once More.” Performed by Carpenters. Now & Then, A&M Records, 1973. APA 7th ed. Carpenter, R., & Bettis, J. (1973). Yesterday once more [Song]. On Now & Then. A&M Records. 正文引用示例：(Carpenter & Bettis, 1973) 版权与合理使用说明（节选自原讲义） “Yesterday Once More” © 1973 words and music by Richard Carpenter and John Bettis. Sound recording © 1973 A&M Records, now under Universal Music Group. All rights are reserved by the copyright holders. This sheet reproduces the lyrics solely for non-commercial, educational use in a university English writing course. 根据美国版权法合理使用条款（17 U.S.C. §107），为评论、教学、学术之目的可有限引用受版权保护的歌词片段；在分析中简短引用（数行）并注明出处通常属于合理使用范围。原讲义明确要求：整首歌词仅限本课程内部学术使用，不得公开出版、售卖或分发。因此本博客不转载完整歌词，仅作学术性引用与点评。 歌词节选（合理使用范围内的短摘录） When I was young I’d listen to the radioWaiting for my favorite songsWhen they played I’d sing alongIt made me smile Every sha-la-la-la / Every wo-o-wo-o / Still shinesEvery shing-a-ling-a-ling / That they’re starting to sing / So fine 编者点评：为什么选这首歌做批判性阅读素材？《Yesterday Once More》之所以成为批判性阅读（critical reading）课堂上的经典素材，关键在于它**”简单中藏复杂”**——表面是一首关于怀旧的流行情歌，但可供分析的语言学与文化层面非常多： 叙事视角：全程第一人称”我”，把怀旧锚定在个体记忆而非宏大公共叙事。这恰是练习 Description（描述文本”如何说”）时，区分”文本说了什么”与”文本怎样说”的好切口。 无意义音节的功能：副歌的 “sha-la-la-la” “wo-o-wo-o” 不传递语义，却模拟了老唱片的拟声质感——这是”形式即内容”的范例，值得在 Interpretation（阐释）中展开。 互文与媒介自觉：Bridge 段的 1960s oldies medley 让歌曲从”谈论旧音乐”变为”直接放出旧音乐”，打破了纯叙述，是通俗文化里的”元文本”手法。 年代错位：1973 年发行的歌，却用温暖女中音与复古编曲营造”比实际更老”的听感——提示我们”怀旧”是一种被建构的审美，而非单纯回忆。 情感的两面性：温暖与略带伤感并存——“so much has changed”让回忆既是慰藉也是刺痛，这正是 bittersweet（苦乐参半）的核心。 也正因如此，它非常适合套用 R-D-I（Restatement–Description–Interpretation） 三步法来做拆解——这一点在后续的 Part A 分析里会得到完整呈现。

posts.title: 小组反思 · Part B（Reflection）
posts.text: 编者按（Cheukwang Hau）：本篇是课程作业 Part B 的原文存档——我们小组（选题：歌曲《Yesterday Once More》）五位成员各自写下”读—写”体验的反思。以下正文为小组成员原始提交内容，一字未改地保留；末尾”编者点评”是我（组长/博主）事后的归纳与再思考。 Reflection from each and every group numbers is as follows:（The ranking is in no particular order） YanWen Chen / 陈彦文（原文仅署名，未展开内容。） Shanyu Liang / 梁善予From the read-to-write experience, I have learned that accumulation is the basis of our critical writing. When reading a research paper, we can not just understand the content of the text, but observe how the author presents arguments and accumulate some common structures useful for our own writing. What’s more, every word of the research paper should be carefully considered, because each word implies the author’s attitude and affects the scientific nature and rigour. Besides, we should pay attention to the use of linking words, which make the logic of our paper clearer. Finally, forming the habit of critical reading and thinking is beneficial to our lives. We can associate the phenomenon of the paper with profound causes. This ability adds greater depth and practical significance to our writing. XIanhui Wang / 汪贤辉In this reading-to-write project, our group chose the song Yesterday Once More. As we went through its lyrics, I learned some natural, everyday expressions, including long-lost friend, look back on and years gone by. Apart from native expressions, the lyrics also gave me fresh ideas about writing. I’ve found that good writing does not always depend on fancy words or complex sentences. We can share our feelings with concrete images like radios, old songs and familiar melodies. It works well if we notice small details and express our thoughts in simple, smooth language. On the other hand, this activity changed how I listen to music. Before, I usually just enjoyed the melody and seldom thought deeply about what a song tries to tell us. But in this project, I figured out its core idea: nostalgia does not mean staying stuck in the past, memories bring us soft comfort. Last but not least, this group work helped me realize that English reading and writing, are far more than memorizing vocabulary or translating sentences. We need to feel the emotions behind the words, and think carefully about how our memories connect with the present. Zhuohong Hou / 侯卓宏Needless to say, learning the course of Critical Reading has taught me a lot of useful vocabulary such as exploitative, stance, utilize and so on and some useful expression like “it is my contention that” which is a useful expression to argue that perspective that you want to argue. What most important is that I realize that reading or writing is not picking every words into a context but connecting each words with “R-D-I”(Restatement-Description-Interpretation) to express your critical thinking. So I will regard “R-D-I” logic flow as a useful tool to get author’s exact conveys and express my critical thinking and apply it on my next writing and reading. Not only is the course of critical reading an English class that taught me many English skills, it also conveys me to an thinking mode which is critical thinking, an ability to explore “from say to mean”(say-do-mean). Zhaoqi Wang / 王昭麒From this activity ,I learn that we don’t just need to learn English as a new language.What’s more,you should understand it as a culture. Maybe it is different from our culture, but we should learn to understand, respect and accept it. Each of his words has different meanings. Before I came into contact with critical reading, my study of English was limited to memorizing words and reading. Just to complete the questions, and after I learned critical reading, I began to face my views on English, and no longer studied for the sake of doing questions to get points. Many articles seem to be just simple narratives and discussions, but in fact they imply personal attitudes and cultural tendencies. Reading with critical thinking can help me jump out of the surface of the text, see the deeper expression logic, and avoid one-sided and shallow understanding. 编者点评（组长归纳）五份反思虽短，却共同勾勒出这门课的核心收益——英语写作课最终教的不是语言技巧，而是批判性思维。我把它收敛成四条共识： 从”工具性学习”到”文化性理解”：汪贤辉、王昭麒都经历了从”背单词/刷题”到”把英语当文化来理解、尊重与接纳”的转变。英语不再是得分工具，而是理解另一种思维方式的窗口。 R-D-I 框架的内化：侯卓宏明确把 Restatement–Description–Interpretation 当作可迁移的”思维工具”，并进一步提炼出 say–do–mean（从”说—做—意”）的批判性路径——这正是课程最想植入的认知习惯。 具体意象胜过华丽辞藻：梁善予、汪贤辉都提到，用 radio、old songs、familiar melodies 这类具体意象去承载情感，比堆砌 fancy words 更有效。这对写作很有启发。 批判性阅读溢出课堂：梁善予把论文现象关联到深层成因，王昭麒学会跳出文本表面看表达逻辑——批判性思维开始反哺对生活与信息的判断。 一点小遗憾：陈彦文（YanWen Chen）部分在原文档中仅有署名、未展开内容。若日后补全，这组反思会更完整。

posts.title: 批判性阅读分析 · Part A（R-D-I）
posts.text: 编者按（Cheukwang Hau）：本篇是课程作业 Part A 的原文存档，作者为本人（Cheukwang Hau）。采用 R-D-I 三步法（Restatement 复述 → Description 描述 → Interpretation 阐释）对《Yesterday Once More》歌词做批判性阅读。以下正文为本人原创提交内容，一字未改地保留；末尾的”编者点评”才是我（作为博主/编者）事后回看时的再思考，两者界限明确，请勿混淆。 RestatementThe song is about a speaker’s memories of old songs. When young, the speaker used to listen to the radio, waiting for favourite songs and singing along. Now those old songs are back again, just like a long-lost friend, and every “sha-la-la” still shines. When the old songs reach the part where he is breaking her heart, the speaker can really cry, just like before. Looking back on the good times of years gone by makes today seem rather sad, because so much has changed, but the speaker still remembers every word of those old melodies. In the end, it is yesterday once more. DescriptionThe song focuses on personal first-person memory instead of public events. It makes the feeling of nostalgia stay in one person’s inner world. In the chorus, there are no clear words but meaningless sounds like “sha-la-la-la”. These sounds do not carry special meanings. They just sound like old records. In the middle part of the song, we can hear a mix of popular songs from the 1960s. At this point, the song is no longer talking about old music. It shows the old music directly to listeners. Besides, the warm and soft alto voice and the retro music style also help. All these things make the song sound older than it really is, though it came out in 1973. InterpretationAfter listening to such a warm yet slightly sad song, it can be argued that the songwriters aim not only to describe everyday scenes — the radio, the old songs and the “sha-la-la-la” refrains — but also to write down memories of the past. These memories are more than a record of “the good times” of “years gone by”: they give the speaker the strength to face the present, because “all my best memories” still “come back clearly” whenever the old songs are played. However, the song is not simply comforting. Looking back also “makes today seem rather sad,” since “so much has changed.” In other words, the song suggests that remembering is bittersweet: the old songs return “just like a long lost friend,” yet they can only return as “yesterday once more” — never as today. 编者点评（事后回看）重读自己这篇 R-D-I，整体结构是规范的，几处观察也站得住脚，挑几点说： 做得扎实的地方 三步法执行到位：Restatement 忠实不添加、Description 聚焦文本特征、Interpretation 落到个人阐释，三者分工清楚，是合格的批判性阅读范式。 Description 有两个真亮点：一是点出 “sha-la-la-la” 无意义却能唤起老唱片质感——抓住了”形式即内容”；二是发现 medley 让歌曲从”谈论旧音乐”转为”直接呈现旧音乐”，这个媒介自觉的观察很细腻。 Interpretation 收尾有力：把怀旧读成 bittersweet，既看到”面对当下的力量”，也承认”物是人非的伤感”，并以 “yesterday once more” 而非 “today” 收束，点出了怀旧的本质局限。 可再深化的方向（建设性） Description 段其实可以再区分一下叙事里的性别化线索——“he’s breaking her heart” 暗示了一种传统的男性叙事视角，值得点一句。 Interpretation 若想更厚，可以联系 1973 年的时代背景（越战尾声、经济滞胀）来读”怀旧”是否也是对动荡当下的一种逃避，而不只是个人感伤。 总体是一篇可以当范文的 R-D-I，结构比辞藻更重要。
